chapter: Raymond Scott, Kirby and postwar bands
title: Apollo shows with the Cotton Club dancers and Harlem hits
summary: Barnet's band backs the Cotton Club dancers at the Apollo and records 'Tappin' at the Tapper' and 'East Side, West Side', jukebox hits in Harlem.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: We played the Apollo Theatre, as I said, 21 times, and we worked with the original Cotton Club Boys and Girls, and their names, I can't think of them all right now -- you know Honey Cole, was one of them.

Yeah, Charlie Atkinson -- great dancers, and the girls' names I can't remember. Beautiful shows, and we had black and white shows. But of course, Barnet had made -- da da da -- mpton Poppin Turnpike was one of the big hits in Harlem, and another thing we made was -- oh, what was the name of it -- yeah, Tappin' at the Tapper.
Why don't we take a break for a minute, just to give you a break.
Okay, Cliff, what was that song you were saying?
Oh yeah, it was on every juke box in Harlem.
That's when we also made East Side, West Side -- and everybody in Harlem was just, and I've seen them and I'm sure you have, too; I've seen them drop off the balcony at the Apollo Theatre.
